title.zh: 第八 祭祀中 北郊 明堂 辟雍 靈臺 迎氣 增祀 六宗 老子
title.en: Volume 98: Rituals and Worship Part Two
title.raw: 第八 祭祀中 北郊 明堂 辟雍 靈臺 迎氣 增祀 六宗 老子 Volume 98: Rituals and Worship Part Two

sentences.zh: 志第八 祭祀中

translations.literal: Treatise Eight: Sacrifices, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 8: Sacrifices, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 北郊 明堂 辟雍 灵臺 迎气 增祀 六宗 老子

translations.literal: Northern suburb; Bright Hall; Biyong; Spirit Terrace; welcoming the seasonal ethers; expanded sacrifices; Six Honored Powers; Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Northern suburban rites, the Bright Hall, the Biyong academy, the Spirit Terrace, welcoming the seasonal qi, supplemental cults, the Six Honored Powers, and worship of Laozi.

sentences.zh: 是年初营北郊，明堂、辟雍、灵台未用事。

translations.literal: That year they first laid out the northern suburb; the Bright Hall, Biyong, and Spirit Terrace had not yet been put to use.
translations.idiomatic: In that year work began on the northern suburban altar, while the Bright Hall, Biyong, and Spirit Terrace were still not in active use.

sentences.zh: 迁吕太后于园。

translations.literal: They moved Empress Dowager Lü to a garden [tomb].
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lü’s spirit seat was removed to an outlying cemetery shrine.

sentences.zh: 上簿太后尊号曰高皇后，当配地，郊高庙。

translations.literal: The Sovereign recorded the Empress Dowager’s honorific title as Empress Gao; she was to match Earth and sacrifice at Gaodi’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor registered her posthumous style as Empress Gao, pairing her with Earth at the northern rite and honoring her at Gaodi’s suburban temple.

sentences.zh: 语在《光武纪》。

translations.literal: The account is in the “Annals of Guangwu.”
translations.idiomatic: The details appear in the annals of Emperor Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 北效在雒阳城北四里，为方坛四陛。

translations.literal: The northern suburb was four li north of Luoyang city; they made a square mound with four stairways.
translations.idiomatic: The northern suburban site lay four li north of Luoyang, laid out as a square altar with four flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 三十三年正月辛未，郊。

translations.literal: On xinwei of the first month of the thirty-third year, they performed the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the first month of Jianwu 33 (57 CE), the court held the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 别祀地祇、位南面西上，高皇后配，西面北上，皆在坛上，地理群神从食，皆在坛下，如元始中故事。

translations.literal: They separately sacrificed to Earth’s numen; positions faced south with precedence to the west; Empress Gao was correlative, facing west with precedence to the north; all were on the mound; terrestrial spirits sharing the offerings were all below the mound, according to the Yuanshi-era precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Earth received a distinct cult on the terrace, stations facing south with senior rank to the west, while Empress Gao stood as consort facing west to the north; terrestrial deities who shared the offerings stood below the mound, following Western Han practice under Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 中岳在未，四岳各在其方孟辰之地，中营内。

translations.literal: The Central Marchmount was at wei; the four marchmounts each were at their direction’s first chen position, inside the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Song stood at the wei compass point, and each of the four outer marchmounts occupied the “first-chen” slot for its quarter—all within the inner camp.

sentences.zh: 海在东；

translations.literal: The sea was in the east;
translations.idiomatic: The sea god was placed on the east;

sentences.zh: 西渎河西，济北，淮来，江南；

translations.literal: the western channel-rivers: west of the Yellow River, north of the Ji, Huai coming, south of the Yangzi;
translations.idiomatic: the western rivers ran west of the Yellow River, north of the Ji, with the Huai approaching from the east and the Yangzi to the south;

sentences.zh: 他山川各如其方，皆在外营内。

translations.literal: Other mountains and rivers each according to their direction, all were inside the outer enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Other hills and streams were assigned to their proper quarters, all within the outer precinct.

sentences.zh: 四陛□及中外营门封神如南郊。

translations.literal: The four stairways [lacuna] and inner and outer enclosure gate enfeoffed spirits were like the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The four stairways, the inner and outer gates, and the gate deities matched the southern suburban layout.

sentences.zh: 地祇、高后用犊各一头，五岳共牛一头，海、四渎共牛一头，群神共二头。

translations.literal: Earth’s numen and Empress Gao each used one calf; the five marchmounts shared one ox; sea and four channel-rivers shared one ox; the host of spirits shared two head.
translations.idiomatic: Earth and Empress Gao each received a calf; the five marchmounts shared one ox, the sea and four great rivers another, and the lesser gods two oxen between them.

sentences.zh: 奏乐亦如南郊。

translations.literal: Performing music was also like the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The musical program duplicated that of the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 既送神，瘗俎实于坛北。

translations.literal: After sending off the spirits, they buried the stand’s meat offerings north of the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirits had been dismissed, the meat from the sacrificial stands was interred north of the altar.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，永平二年正月辛未，初祀五帝于明堂，光武帝配。

translations.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, on xinwei of the first month of Yongping 2, they first sacrificed to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall, with Guangwudi as correlative.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming’s accession, on the xinwei day of the first month of Yongping 2 (59 CE), the court first offered to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall, with Emperor Guangwu as joint recipient.

sentences.zh: 五帝坐位堂上，各处其方。

translations.literal: The Five Thearchs’ seats were on the hall above, each occupying its direction.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Thearchs sat on the upper hall, each in his own cosmic quarter.

sentences.zh: 黄帝在未，皆如南郊之位。

translations.literal: The Yellow Thearch was at wei; all were like the southern suburb’s positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Thearch occupied the wei position, the same arrangement as at the southern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 光武帝位在青帝之南少退，西面。

translations.literal: Guangwudi’s position was south of the Green Thearch, slightly set back, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu’s seat stood just south of the Green Thearch, set slightly behind it, facing west.

sentences.zh: 牲各一犊，奏乐如南郊。

translations.literal: Each victim was one calf; performing music was like the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Each deity received a calf, and the musicians followed the southern suburban score.

sentences.zh: 卒事，遂升灵台，以望云物。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, then they ascended the Spirit Terrace to observe clouds and prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, they climbed the Spirit Terrace to scan the sky for omens.

sentences.zh: 迎时气，五郊之兆。

translations.literal: Welcoming the seasonal ethers: the five suburbs’ precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the seasonal qi: the five suburban altar sites.

sentences.zh: 自永平中，以《礼谶》及《月令》有五郊迎气服色，因采元始中故事，兆五郊于雒阳四方。

translations.literal: From within Yongping, because the *Rites Apocrypha* and the *Monthly Ordinances* had five suburbs’ welcoming-the-ether garment colors, therefore adopting Yuanshi-era precedents, they laid out five suburbs on Luoyang’s four sides.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era the court, citing the ritual apocrypha and the *Monthly Ordinances* on the five suburban welcomes and their prescribed colors, followed Yuanshi precedents and marked out five suburban sites around Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 中兆在未，坛皆三尺，阶无等。

translations.literal: The central precinct was at wei; the mounds were all three chi; the steps had no ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The central altar stood at wei, each mound rose three feet, and the steps had no staggered tiers.

sentences.zh: 立春之日，迎春于东郊，祭青帝句芒。

translations.literal: On the day Establishing Spring, they welcomed spring at the eastern suburb and sacrificed to the Green Thearch Gou Mang.
translations.idiomatic: On the Beginning of Spring they greeted the season at the eastern suburb with offerings to the Green Thearch and his minister Gou Mang.

sentences.zh: 车旗服饰皆青。

translations.literal: Carriages, banners, garments, and ornaments were all green.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, flags, and court dress were all green.

sentences.zh: 歌《青阳》，八佾舞《云翘》之舞。

translations.literal: They sang “Green Yang”; eight rows danced the “Cloud Crest” dance.
translations.idiomatic: They sang *Qingyang* and performed the eight-row *Yunqiao* dance.

sentences.zh: 及因赐文官太傅、司徒以下缣各有差。

translations.literal: Moreover thereby they bestowed on civil officials from the Grand Tutor and Minister of Education downward silk in graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials from the Grand Tutor and Minister of Education on down were then given graded gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 立夏之日，迎夏于南郊，祭赤帝祝融。

translations.literal: On the day Establishing Summer, they welcomed summer at the southern suburb and sacrificed to the Red Thearch Zhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: On the Beginning of Summer they received the season at the southern suburb with offerings to the Red Thearch and Zhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 车旗服饰皆赤。

translations.literal: Carriages, banners, garments, and ornaments were all red.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, flags, and dress were all red.

sentences.zh: 歌《朱明》，八佾舞《云翘》之舞。

translations.literal: They sang “Red Brightness”; eight rows danced the “Cloud Crest” dance.
translations.idiomatic: They sang *Zhuming* and danced the eight-row *Yunqiao*.

sentences.zh: 先立秋十八日，迎黄灵于中北，祭黄帝后土。

translations.literal: Eighteen days before Establishing Autumn, they welcomed the Yellow Spirit north of the center and sacrificed to the Yellow Thearch and Sovereign Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen days before the Beginning of Autumn they welcomed the Yellow Spirit between the central and northern sites, offering to the Yellow Thearch and Hou Tu.

sentences.zh: 车旗服饰皆黄。

translations.literal: Carriages, banners, garments, and ornaments were all yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, flags, and vestments were all yellow.

sentences.zh: 歌《朱明》，八佾舞《云翘》、《育命》之舞。

translations.literal: They sang “Red Brightness”; eight rows danced the “Cloud Crest” and “Nurturing the Mandate” dances.
translations.idiomatic: They sang *Zhuming* and presented the eight-row *Yunqiao* and *Yuming* dances.

sentences.zh: 立秋之日，迎秋于西郊，祭白帝蓐收。

translations.literal: On the day Establishing Autumn, they welcomed autumn at the western suburb and sacrificed to the White Thearch Ru Shou.
translations.idiomatic: On the Beginning of Autumn they greeted the season at the western suburb, sacrificing to the White Thearch and Ru Shou.

sentences.zh: 车旗服饰皆白。

translations.literal: Carriages, banners, garments, and ornaments were all white.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, banners, and attire were all white.

sentences.zh: 歌《西皓》，八佾舞《育命》之舞。

translations.literal: They sang “Western Radiance”; eight rows danced the “Nurturing the Mandate” dance.
translations.idiomatic: They sang *Xihao* and performed the eight-row *Yuming* dance.

sentences.zh: 使谒者以一特牲先祭先虞于坛，有事，天子入囿射牲，以祭宗庙，名曰貙刘。

translations.literal: They ordered a herald with one specially raised victim first to sacrifice to the Forerunner-of-the-Hunt on the mound; when there was the affair, the Son of Heaven entered the park and shot the victim, to sacrifice to the ancestral temples; it was named the chu-liu.
translations.idiomatic: A herald offered a single bullock to the hunting god on the mound beforehand; on the appointed day the emperor entered the royal park, shot the sacrificial beast himself, and the meat was forwarded to the ancestral shrines—the autumn rite known as the *chu-liu*.

sentences.zh: 语在《礼仪志》。

translations.literal: The account is in the “Treatise on Rites and Ceremonial.”
translations.idiomatic: The procedure is set out in the treatise on ritual.

sentences.zh: 立冬之日，迎冬于北郊，祭黑帝玄冥。

translations.literal: On the day Establishing Winter, they welcomed winter at the northern suburb and sacrificed to the Black Thearch Xuan Ming.
translations.idiomatic: On the Beginning of Winter they received the season at the northern suburb with offerings to the Black Thearch and Xuan Ming.

sentences.zh: 车旗服饰皆黑。

translations.literal: Carriages, banners, garments, and ornaments were all black.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots, standards, and robes were all black.

sentences.zh: 歌《玄冥》，八佾舞《育命》之舞。

translations.literal: They sang “Dark Obscurity”; eight rows danced the “Nurturing the Mandate” dance.
translations.idiomatic: They sang *Xuanming* and danced the eight-row *Yuming*.

sentences.zh: 章帝即位，元和二年正月，诏曰：「山川百神，应祀者未尽。

translations.literal: When Zhangdi took the throne, in the first month of Yuanhe 2, an edict said, “Mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits—those who ought to be sacrificed to are not yet exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhangdi’s reign, in the first month of Yuanhe 2 (85 CE), an edict declared: “Among mountains, rivers, and the myriad gods, many who deserve cult have yet to receive it.”

sentences.zh: 其议增修群祀宜享祀者。」

translations.literal: Deliberate on increasing and repairing mass sacrifices for those fit to receive sacrifice.”
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministers debate which communal shrines should be enlarged or newly endowed.”

sentences.zh: 二月，上东巡狩，将至泰山，道使使者奉一太牢祠帝尧于济阴成阳灵台。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Sovereign toured east on the hunt; when about to reach Mount Tai, on the way he sent envoys bearing one grand sacrifice to sacrifice to Emperor Yao at the Spirit Terrace of Chengyang in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor set out on an eastern tour; before reaching Mount Tai he dispatched envoys with a full *tailao* offering to honor Emperor Yao at the Spirit Terrace in Chengyang, Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 上至泰山，修光武山南坛兆。

translations.literal: The Sovereign arrived at Mount Tai and repaired Guangwu’s southern-mountain altar precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Mount Tai he restored the southern-altar site that Guangwu had established.

sentences.zh: 辛未，柴祭天地群神如故事。

translations.literal: On xinwei, they performed the firewood sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the host of spirits according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he offered the *chai* burnt sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, and the full pantheon, following established form.

sentences.zh: 壬申，宗祀五帝于孝武所作汶上明堂，光武帝配，如雒阳明堂礼。

translations.literal: On renshen, they performed the lineal sacrifice to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall on the Wen that Xiaowu had built, with Guangwudi as correlative, like the Luoyang Bright Hall ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he offered the lineal sacrifice to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall above the Wen River built by Emperor Wu, pairing Guangwu as at the Luoyang Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，更告祀高祖、太宗、世宗、中宗、世祖、显宗于明堂，各一太牢。

translations.literal: On guiyou, they further announced sacrifice to Gaozu, Taizong, Shizong, Zhongzong, Shizu, and Xianzong in the Bright Hall, each one grand sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he reported separately to Gaozu, Taizong, Shizong, Zhongzong, Shizu, and Xianzong in the Bright Hall, each with a full *tailao*.

sentences.zh: 卒事，遂觐东后，飨赐王侯群臣。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, then they had audience with the Eastern Empress and feasted and bestowed on kings, marquises, and the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremonies ended, he presented himself to the empress and gave a banquet for the kings, marquises, and officials.

sentences.zh: 因行郡国，幸鲁，祠东海恭王，及孔子七十二弟子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he traveled commanderies and kingdoms, favored Lu, sacrificed to the Respectful Prince of the Eastern Sea, and to Confucius’s seventy-two disciples.
translations.idiomatic: He then toured the provinces, visited Lu, sacrificed to Prince Gong of Eastern Sea, and to Confucius’s seventy-two disciples.

sentences.zh: 四月，还京都。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚申，告至，祠高庙、世祖，各一特牛。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he announced arrival and sacrificed to Gaodi’s temple and Shizu, each one specially raised ox.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he reported his return and offered a specially raised bull each at the shrines to Emperor Gao and Shizu.

sentences.zh: 又为灵台十二门作诗，各以其月祀而奏之。

translations.literal: Also for the Spirit Terrace’s twelve gates he made poems; each according to its month sacrificed and performed them.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed hymns for the twelve gates of the Spirit Terrace, one for each month’s sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 和帝无所增改。

translations.literal: Hedi added or changed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He altered none of this.

sentences.zh: 安帝即位，元初六年，以《尚书》欧阳家说，谓六宗者，在天地四方之中，为上下四方之宗。

translations.literal: When Andi took the throne, in Yuanchu 6, following the Ouyang school’s explanation in the *Documents*, they held that the Six Honored Powers are in the midst of Heaven and Earth and the four directions, being the ancestors of above, below, and the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An, in Yuanchu 6 (119 CE), the court adopted the Ouyang reading of the *Book of Documents*, defining the Six Honored Powers as the spirits of the zenith, nadir, and four quarters—the axes between Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 以元始中故事，谓六宗《易》六子之气日、月、雷公、风伯、山、泽者为非是。

translations.literal: Regarding the Yuanshi-era precedent that called the Six Honored Powers the *Changes* six sons’ ethers—sun, moon, Thunder Duke, Wind Earl, mountain, marsh—to be not correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Han Yuanshi definition—which equated the Six Honored Powers with the six lines’ pneumas of the *Zhouyi*, namely sun, moon, thunder, wind, mountain, and marsh—was rejected as wrong.

sentences.zh: 三月庚辰，初更立六宗，祀于雒阳西北戍亥之地，礼比太社也。

translations.literal: On gengchen of the third month, they first anew established the Six Honored Powers, sacrificing northwest of Luoyang in the xu-hai ground; the ritual compared to Grand Earth’s.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the third month they first re-established the Six Honored Powers at a site northwest of Luoyang between the xu and hai compass sectors, with rites modeled on the Great Earth sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 延光三年，上东巡狩，至泰山，柴祭，及祠汶上明堂，如元和二年故事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanguang, the Sovereign toured east on the hunt, arrived at Mount Tai, performed the firewood sacrifice, and sacrificed to the Bright Hall on the Wen, like the Yuanhe 2 precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanguang 3 (124 CE) the emperor toured east to Mount Tai, offered the *chai* sacrifice, and worshipped at the Bright Hall above the Wen River, repeating the Yuanhe 2 program.

sentences.zh: 顺帝即位，修奉常祀。

translations.literal: When Shundi took the throne, he repaired the Director of Ceremonies’ sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun, on his accession, restored the regular state sacrifices overseen by the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 桓帝即位十八年，好神仙事。

translations.literal: Huandi, eighteen years after taking the throne, favored transcendents’ affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen years into Emperor Huan’s reign he became devoted to occult and immortalist pursuits.

sentences.zh: 延熹八年，初使中常侍之陈国苦县祠老子。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yanxi, for the first time he sent a Regular Palace Attendant to Ku county in Chen state to sacrifice to Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 8 (165 CE) he first dispatched a Regular Palace Attendant to Ku in the princedom of Chen to sacrifice at Laozi’s shrine.

sentences.zh: 九年，亲祠老子于濯龙。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he personally sacrificed to Laozi at Zhuolong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he worshipped Laozi in person at the Zhuolong lodge in the palace.

sentences.zh: 文罽为坛，饰淳金钅□器，设华盖之坐，用郊天乐也。

translations.literal: Patterned wool served as the mound; they ornamented pure gold [lacuna] vessels; they set up a flowered canopy seat; they used suburban Heaven music.
translations.idiomatic: They spread figured carpets for an altar, set out vessels of refined gold, placed a dais beneath a jeweled canopy, and used the same musical suite as at the suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
